title: Model Hosting Cyber Insurance & Liability Exhibit (template)
body:
Purpose and scope:
This exhibit is intended to be attached to customer-facing model hosting, dedicated, or private deployment agreements where the Supplier (Redwood Inference or affiliate) is providing model hosting, inference runtime, or managed infrastructure. The exhibit sets minimum cyber insurance requirements, allocates incident response and remediation costs, and clarifies liability caps and exceptions specific to model weights, inference outputs, and subprocessor activities.

How to use this template:
- Insert into SOW or Master Services Agreement as an Exhibit.
- Populate the bracketed fields and cross-reference the counterparty's insurance schedules.
- Use negotiation notes in square brackets; legal should clear changes that expand Redwood operational obligations.

1) Definitions (selected)
- "Affected Data": Customer data and prompts, including transient inference inputs retained in caches or logs for debugging.
- "Model Weights": the trained model binaries, quantized artifacts, and derivative artifacts hosted or served by Supplier.
- "Incident": a security event or data breach resulting in unauthorized access, disclosure, modification, or destruction of Affected Data or Model Weights.
- "Direct Incident Costs": reasonably incurred third-party forensic, legal, regulatory notification, credit monitoring, and remediation costs attributable to a Supplier Incident.
- "Supplier Incident": an Incident caused by the Supplier's failure to meet contractual security obligations or by Supplier-operated infrastructure, excluding incidents solely caused by Customer misconfiguration or Customer-controlled keys.

2) Insurance (minimum coverages and evidence)
- Supplier shall maintain, at its own expense, the following insurance coverages with insurers with an AM Best rating of A- or better:
  - Commercial General Liability (CGL): $5,000,000 per occurrence / $5,000,000 aggregate.
  - Technology Errors & Omissions / Professional Liability: $5,000,000 per claim / $5,000,000 aggregate, covering errors in model serving and api delivery.
  - Cyber & Privacy Liability (including network security, privacy breach, regulatory fines where insurable, and media liability): $10,000,000 per incident / $10,000,000 aggregate. Coverage must include coverage for forensic investigation, regulatory defense, notification costs, business interruption (incl. cloud-hosting interruption), and the cost of restoring corrupted Model Weights.
  - Crime / Employee Dishonesty: $1,000,000 (if Supplier personnel have administrative access to Customer data or keys).
- Supplier shall provide Customer with certificates of insurance and policy summaries within 10 business days of Effective Date and upon each policy renewal.
- Any self-insured retention (SIR) or deductible above $250,000 requires Customer consent (not to be unreasonably withheld).

3) Allocation of costs following a Supplier Incident
- Direct Incident Costs: Supplier will promptly pay or reimburse Customer for Direct Incident Costs up to the limits of policy coverage and subject to the Liability Cap below. Supplier shall not seek reimbursement from Customer for reasonable third-party incident response costs where Supplier is the proximate cause.
- Forensic & Restoration: Supplier is responsible for forensic investigation costs and costs to restore or re‑train Model Weights that have been corrupted or made unusable as a direct result of Supplier negligence. If restoration requires Customer-supplied training data, Supplier may recover documented, reasonable re-training compute costs from Customer only where Customer requested new model training independent of Supplier negligence.
- Business Interruption & SLA Credits: Supplier's obligation for business interruption is limited to the SLA credit schedule in the Agreement. Business interruption claims exceeding SLA credits may be recoverable under Cyber insurance or as specified below in Liability Exceptions.

4) Liability cap and exceptions
- Liability Cap: Except for the exceptions below, Supplier's aggregate liability to Customer for all claims arising out of or relating to the Agreement (including exhibits) will not exceed the greater of: (i) $10,000,000; or (ii) 12 months of fees paid by Customer to Supplier under the Agreement.
- Exceptions (no cap): The Liability Cap does not apply to: (a) Customer's indemnifiable losses arising from Supplier's gross negligence or willful misconduct; (b) obligations to pay third-party amounts where Supplier has expressly agreed to assume indemnity (see Indemnities); (c) Supplier's obligations for direct regulatory fines and penalties to the extent not precluded by law from being covered by insurance and to the extent such fines are not subject to an insurance exclusion; (d) breaches leading to material theft of Model Weights or proprietary model IP where Supplier's negligence is the proximate cause.
- Note: Customer should be advised that some regulatory fines (e.g., GDPR administrative fines) may be uninsurable in some jurisdictions; allocation should consider that reality.

5) Subprocessor and third-party hosted models
- Subprocessor Incidents: Where an Incident is caused by a subprocessor engaged by Supplier (e.g., cloud provider, external model host), Supplier remains primarily responsible for remediation and Direct Incident Costs, but Supplier may seek recovery from the subprocessor as permitted by Supplier's contract with that subprocessor.
- Chain of Insurance: Supplier must represent that it will use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain flow-down insurance or indemnities from subprocessors. Supplier will provide Customer a written summary of subprocessor insurance upon request (subject to redaction for commercial terms).

6) Indemnities (customer-facing template language)
- Supplier Indemnity: Supplier will defend and indemnify Customer against third-party Claims to the extent arising from Supplier's negligence, willful misconduct, or breach of its security obligations resulting in unauthorized disclosure of Affected Data. Supplier's obligation includes settlement amounts and defense costs, subject to the Liability Cap except where an exception applies.
- Customer Indemnity: Customer will indemnify Supplier for Claims arising from Customer-supplied content that violates law or third-party rights, or Customer configuration changes that cause outages.

7) Incident notification, cooperation & evidence preservation
- Notification: Supplier will notify Customer within 48 hours of becoming aware of a Supplier Incident materially affecting Customer's Affected Data or Model Weights.
- Incident Plan: Supplier will provide an incident summary within 5 business days and a remediation plan within 10 business days, including a timeline for forensic activities and expected costs.
- Preservation: Supplier will not alter or destroy logs, backups, or forensic artifacts without Customer's consent (consent not to be unreasonably withheld) and will preserve evidence for a minimum of 180 days after an Incident unless required by law to retain longer.
- Communications: Public disclosures or joint press statements require mutual agreement; however, Supplier may issue narrow technical disclosures to regulators as required by law after notice to Customer.

8) Settlement approvals and subrogation
- Reasonable settlement: Supplier will not settle any third-party Claim that admits fault and imposes obligations on Customer without Customer's prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld).
- Subrogation: Supplier waives rights of subrogation against Customer except where Customer is the proximate cause of the Incident.

9) Audit & proof of coverage
- Supplier will furnish copies of insurance certificates and, upon Customer request and subject to confidentiality, policy declarations and endorsements showing coverage for cyber incidents and model restoration.
- Where Customer requires, Supplier will agree to a one-time limited audit of its insurance program by an independent auditor for high-risk customers, the scope and cost of which will be mutually agreed.

10) Negotiation notes & open questions (internal)
- Is $10M cyber liability sufficient for high-reg model hosting customers? Consider a tiered approach: e.g., $10M for SMB, $25M+ for enterprise with sensitive data.
- Confirm that policy language will cover costs to re-train or re-generate Model Weights (may be excluded by some carriers). Add explicit language that costs to restore model artifacts are covered.
- Deductible negotiation: Customers will push for low SIR; keep SIR negotiation playbook (e.g., Redwood accepts up to $250k; >$250k requires executive sign-off).
- Regulator fines: carriers sometimes exclude regulatory fines; Include carve-in or a cap carve-out in contract (we do elsewhere in DPA templates).
- Subprocessor flow-down: We cannot always obtain matching limits from cloud hyperscalers; ensure clause allows us to seek recovery but accepts practical limits.

11) Example SLA interplay and remediation waterfall (summary)
- Step 1: Consumer suffers outage — apply SLA credits per Agreement (primary remedy for short disruptions).
- Step 2: If outage caused by security incident that results in data exfiltration or material model corruption, Supplier funds forensic and restoration costs (subject to insurance and cap exceptions).
- Step 3: If third-party claim arises, indemnity and cyber insurance layers apply.

Annex A: Template certificate language to provide to customers
- "Insurer: [name of insurer]
  Policy Number: [policy number]
  Coverage Type: Cyber & Privac
  Limits: $10,000,000 per occurrence / $10,000,000 aggregate
  Effective Dates: [mm/dd/yyyy - mm/dd/yyyy]
  Producer Contact: [broker contact]
  Note: Any policy cancellation or material change requires 30 days prior written notice to Customer."

Quick negotiation checklist for Sales/AE/Legal ops:
- Customer tier mapping to insurance minimums (SMB/Early/Enterprise).
- Confirm SIR thresholds and exec escalation path.
- Identify any customer-specific regulatory regimes (e.g., health, financial) that require additional cover.
- Prepare fallback language: if Supplier cannot obtain extended coverage, propose a higher monetary cap instead of higher policy limits.

Revision history & approvals:

[END OF TEMPLATE]

Negotiation log: (notes to self)
- 2024-10-10: Proposed $10M cyber limit pushed back by large fintech prospect; they asked for $25M. Flag for exec escalation.
- 2024-10-24: Legal asked to add explicit model restoration language after carrier feedback.

Unresolved items for legal ops:
- Standardize tiers and map to pricing addenda.
- Create short one-page summary for sales to attach to RFP responses.
- Decide whether to require multinational policy endorsements (territorial scope) for customers with EU regulatory exposure.
